en: dip in flour and egg and fry

does: Rolls shaped pieces of meat mixture in flour, dips them in beaten egg and fries them at once in a layer of hot oil, turning them, until the egg coat is set and golden on every side.

intro.what: Frying in an egg coat dips floured pieces in beaten egg and fries them in a layer of hot oil.
intro.why: It teaches how flour lets an egg coat cling and how a set coat protects a soft mixture.

how: Heat oil in a wide pan to about the depth of a finger.
Beat the eggs in a shallow bowl and spread flour on a plate.
Roll a piece in the flour and tap off the excess, so the egg has something to hold on to.
Dip it in the egg, let the extra drip off, and lay it straight into the hot oil.
Fry it, turning, until the coat is golden on every side, then drain it on paper.

cues.text: A steady sizzle as each piece goes in.
A thin, even, golden coat that clings to the piece with no bare patches.

mistakes.mistake: Dipping in egg without flour first, so that the egg slides off in the pan.
mistakes.fix: Roll the piece in flour first and tap off the excess.

mistakes.mistake: Coating the pieces long before they are fried, so that the coat turns soggy and patchy.
mistakes.fix: Coat each piece just before it goes in the oil.

quiz.question: Why roll the piece in flour before the egg?
choices: So the egg has something to cling to.
quiz.because: A dry flour layer gives the wet egg a surface to hold.

quiz.question: When should a piece be coated?
choices: Just before it goes in the oil.
quiz.because: A coat left waiting turns soggy and falls away.

quiz.question: What does a good coat look like?
choices: Thin, even and golden all round.
quiz.because: An even golden coat shows the egg clung and set.

quiz.question: The egg coat slides off in the pan. What should change?
choices: Flour the pieces first and tap off the excess.
quiz.because: Flour gives the egg a grip.

comes_after.why: The mixture is shaped into pieces of one size before it is coated.

variant_of.differs: The pieces are of a soft meat mixture, rolled in flour and dipped in beaten egg just before they go in, and turned in a deeper layer of oil until the egg coat is set and golden.
